claim_paraphrase: Admissible finite rollout coordinates form an open domain
assumptions: f is C^r on open O; finite N
evidence: Recursive inverse images of O are open; finite composition preserves C^r.

claim_paraphrase: Full-state augmented behavior is an embedded C^r manifold of dimension n+Nm
assumptions: Measured initial state and all future inputs retained; open domain
evidence: After permuting coordinates the rollout is (q,G(q)); identity Jacobian block and continuous projection inverse prove embedding.

claim_paraphrase: Dynamics residuals give a regular level set with codimension Nn
assumptions: Future states retained; f is C^1; open evaluation domain
evidence: Jacobian in future states is lower bidiagonal with identity blocks.
annotation: Independent consistency check of the same graph.

claim_paraphrase: Geometry requires no controllability, stabilizability or dynamics invertibility
assumptions: Full-state coordinates; no inference from sampled data
evidence: The identity block is present even for unstable/uncontrollable transitions.
annotation: Correct; separate from finite-data spanning and control.

evidence: Pull back open D_N by u -> (xbar,u); repeat graph proof.
annotation: This is the ordinary single-shooting search space.

claim_paraphrase: Projection and exact rollout form an exact encoder-decoder pair
evidence: Projection recovers q and recursion recovers its unique states.
annotation: Coordinate restatement; D evaluates the dynamics.

claim_paraphrase: Exact differentiable reconstruction needs latent dimension at least n+Nm
assumptions: C^1 encoder and decoder; differentiable decoder domain; nonempty behavior
evidence: The chain rule factors a rank n+Nm tangent-space identity through R^p.
annotation: Specify smooth domain or neighborhood for A subset R^p; exact statement only.

claim_paraphrase: Approximate restricted-distribution compression is not ruled out
assumptions: Lower bound is for exact C^1 reconstruction
evidence: Approximate reconstruction does not differentiate to the identity.

claim_paraphrase: LTI full-state behavior is a linear subspace with the same dimension
assumptions: Globally defined LTI recursion; full-state data
evidence: Linear rollout retains q, hence is injective.
annotation: This is not an IO finite-data spanning theorem.

claim_paraphrase: An output-only extension requires an observability/injectivity condition
assumptions: Finite output windows must distinguish compatible internal states
evidence: x+ = x, y=0 has behavior dimension Nm; finite lag can restore state distinguishability only under hypotheses.
annotation: The paper flags the issue and proves no nonlinear IO extension.

claim_paraphrase: Held-input sampled flow inherits C^r behavior
assumptions: C^r vector field; trajectories exist over the sample; open flow domain
evidence: Augment with udot=0 and use smooth dependence; compose finite sampled maps.
annotation: Record existence domain, not global existence.

assumptions: Every RK stage lies in the vector-field domain
evidence: Finite evaluations and arithmetic preserve C^r on the stage-admissible open domain.
annotation: Numerical behavior differs from exact-flow behavior; no integration-error guarantee.

assumptions: Box restriction of free coordinates; smooth open ambient chart
evidence: Graph embedding carries the free-coordinate box structure.
annotation: General state constraints require separate regularity.

claim_paraphrase: Adding noise coordinates enlarges the behavior dimension
assumptions: Noise realization must also be retained in the augmented behavior, or its effect must be injective
evidence: If f ignores xi and w includes only x/u, increasing xi dimension leaves the behavior unchanged.
annotation: Clarify augmentation. The graph proof applies to (q,xi,G(q,xi)), not automatically its x/u projection.

claim_paraphrase: Learning, prediction quality and closed-loop stability remain future work
assumptions: Part I establishes exact deterministic full-state geometry only
evidence: The paper explicitly defers these developments to Part II; the implementation composes an ordinary learned transition.
annotation: Do not infer a control guarantee or sample-efficiency bound from Part I.
